saw.short: John Lewis's 2026 Christmas ad stars Kristin Scott Thomas and a talking toy
saw.headline: John Lewis's Christmas ad stars *Kristin Scott Thomas* and a talking toy
saw.what: John Lewis's 20th Christmas ad is out. Per Metro, Kristin Scott Thomas befriends Pickles, a talking toy dog voiced by Paul Whitehouse, to a Sam Fender cover of “You Can't Always Get What You Want”. The tagline is “Don't give up on giving”.
saw.why: The biggest UK Christmas ad gives every brand a conversation to join. Reaction is still building.

saw.short: Sainsbury's brings back the BFG, and Tesco's ad premieres on ITV
saw.headline: Sainsbury's *brings back the BFG*, and Tesco's ad premieres on ITV
saw.what: Sainsbury's brought the BFG back for a third year, with a cold and colleague Annie delivering his feast. Tesco's “The Wrong Address” premiered on ITV on Sunday. A OnePulse poll of about 500 UK adults, taken before each ad's first TV airing, gave Sainsbury's 3.8/5 and Tesco 3.6/5.
saw.why: Supermarket ads get scored within hours. Treat the poll as a quick snapshot.

saw.short: A BBC News graphic reflection reads as a rude word
saw.headline: A BBC News graphic *reflection* reads as a rude word
saw.what: Metro reports that on a weekend BBC News broadcast, the reflection of a “US MIDTERM ELECTIONS” screen behind an anchor looked like a rude word. TV critic Scott Bryan flagged it on X: “BBC News errrr… you might want to check the reflection.” The BBC hadn't commented.
saw.why: Viewers catch on-screen slips fast, and a mirrored graphic was enough. Check reflections in anything you film.

saw.short: Kimi Antonelli becomes the youngest F1 world champion
saw.headline: Kimi Antonelli becomes the *youngest F1 world champion*
saw.what: At 20, Kimi Antonelli clinched the F1 title with third place at the Mexico City Grand Prix on Sunday. He is the youngest champion ever and the first Italian champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953, per F1.com.
saw.why: A first-of-its-kind record gives every account a reason to post.

saw.short: Amanda Holden's Christmas decorations go up in early November
saw.headline: Amanda Holden's *Christmas decorations* go up in early November
saw.what: Amanda Holden, 55, posted an Instagram tour of her Surrey home fully decorated for Christmas, put up by professional decorators over the weekend. Metro says she paid for the installation.
saw.why: “Too early for Christmas?” is a yearly debate. Celebrities start it and brands join in.

platform.short: Instagram is reportedly paying creators up to $500,000 for long-form video
platform.headline: Instagram is *reportedly paying creators* for long-form video
platform.what: Business Insider reports Instagram has offered some creators $50,000, and others six-figure deals up to $500,000, to post long-form video to Features. Meta didn't confirm the figures. A spokesperson said it is “funding Features content directly with some creators”.
platform.why: Instagram is paying to fill a new format. Don't plan around it in the UK yet.
platform.source: Social Media Today, 1 Nov (citing Business Insider)

platform.short: X launches a Video Kickstart Bonus for vertical video
platform.headline: X launches a *Video Kickstart Bonus* for vertical video
platform.what: X is piloting an invite-only bonus: creators who post 15 qualifying vertical videos, each under 3 minutes, on 15 different days in about a month earn a bonus, and are fast-tracked into Original Content Rewards. UK availability isn't stated.
platform.why: X is paying for vertical video. For now it's invite-only.

platform.short: TikTok signs a WTA deal, with an exclusive livestream today
platform.headline: TikTok signs a *WTA deal*, with an exclusive livestream today
platform.what: TikTok will exclusively livestream the WTA Finals draw ceremony today, ahead of the finals in Indian Wells on 8–15 Nov. A “WTA Creator Club” gives creators tournament access. TikTok says the WTA's account has passed 1m followers.
platform.why: Sports bodies are building creator programmes on TikTok, and exclusives make live events a social format.
